title: Control-room daemon transport seam
description:
Objective: make the daemon startable and reachable, and give the control-room client a real transport behind its existing type surface, so the standalone app can be driven against production authority instead of fixtures.

WHY THIS EXISTS (project rail 4, Clause 2 gap measurement). The epic's own architecture note promises the control room is "connected to the daemon through generated authenticated HTTP/query contracts and a resumable cursor stream". Nothing implements that. Measured at planning time:
- NO HTTP LISTENER EXISTS ANYWHERE. grep for createServer(, .listen(, Deno.serve, Bun.serve across apps, packages and adapters (node_modules and tests excluded) returns ZERO.
- THE DAEMON IS NOT A PROCESS. apps/daemon/package.json declares no "main" and no "bin"; its only scripts are typecheck and test. Nothing can start it.
- THE CLIENT HAS NO TRANSPORT. packages/control-room-client exports exactly createCompatGate plus types; grep for fetch(, http, EventSource, url, request across its sources returns ZERO.
- THE APP NEVER CALLS IT. apps/control-room references @moe/control-room-client only through "import type" (data/data-adapter.ts:1, data/data-contract.ts:1). ControlRoomClientSurface is an injectable TYPE with no runtime implementation and no construction site.

NO EXISTING TASK CLOSES THIS, checked before creating:
- task-6c732e0032534cc0abe9196ad467308f "Streamable HTTP adapter" is DONE but is packages/mcp/src/http/** for MCP hosts, and explicitly excludes browser UI APIs.
- task-5e43a9e294ef48fdab23817c8c6cfc45 "Foundation daemon ingress surface" is BACKLOG and publishes EXPORTS; its description states "NOT in scope: behavior changes, fixtures, transport listeners, or new authority". It will not create a listener.

CONSUMERS BLOCKED ON THIS: task-3f503779 (daemon-connected journey harness) and, through it, task-667b1085 (Control-room journey gate).

SCOPE: a startable daemon entry point with a local HTTP listener over the already-committed read and command surfaces, plus a runtime implementation satisfying the existing ControlRoomClientSurface type. Bind to loopback only.

NOT IN SCOPE, each genuinely separate and to be created once this seam's shape is known: the resumable cursor stream; authentication hardening beyond a local loopback guard; and wiring the app's data adapter to construct a live client in place of fixtures. Do not guess at those here.

Owned paths: the daemon entry/listener module, packages/control-room-client transport module, and the manifest entries that make the daemon startable.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test and pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test
definitionOfDone: The daemon is startable as a process: its package declares an entry point, and starting it binds an HTTP listener on LOOPBACK ONLY with a caller-supplied or ephemeral port — never a hardcoded well-known port and never a non-loopback interface. A test starts it, reads the bound port, and shuts it down.

The listener exposes the already-committed daemon read and command surfaces. It introduces NO new authority, NO new command kinds, and NO new refusal vocabulary — it is transport over existing handlers. A test asserts an unknown route and a malformed body are each refused with a specific stable reason code naming the refusing layer, not merely that a non-200 came back.

A runtime implementation satisfies the EXISTING ControlRoomClientSurface type from packages/control-room-client rather than a new parallel interface, so apps/control-room's data-adapter.ts and data-contract.ts type-check against it unchanged.

Clause 1 is satisfied by a real consumer edge, not by exports: an integration test constructs the runtime client, points it at a started daemon, performs one committed read, and asserts the payload matches what the daemon's in-process handler returns for the same input. That equality is the point — it proves the transport is faithful rather than merely responsive.

Startup, port-bind, shutdown and request-refusal failures each return a distinct stable reason code, asserted specifically. The listener closes on EVERY exit path including failure; a leaked listener or port is a defect, and on Windows a surviving handle surfaces later as EBUSY rather than the real error.

Both gates pass — pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test and pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test — and each failure-path test is verified by mutating the production surface and confirming it goes red.
taskRails: Authoritative design: D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-rebuild-design.md SHA-256 1D9D1EC97D3F07247FBBC088045E0BA2FD6DA8307F10A9026C55106419383191; do not edit it. Read its control-room connection section before choosing the route shape, and follow it rather than inventing a protocol.

TRANSPORT ONLY — NO NEW AUTHORITY. This seam serves the committed handlers and nothing else. It may not add a command kind, compute readiness, derive a truth class, or mint a refusal the daemon does not already produce. If a route needs authority that does not exist, that is a prerequisite task, not something to add here.

LOOPBACK ONLY, and no hardcoded well-known port. A development transport that binds a public interface is a security defect, not a convenience. Prefer an ephemeral port reported back to the caller so parallel runs cannot collide.

Do not duplicate packages/mcp/src/http/**. That adapter is DONE and serves the MCP surface for MCP hosts; it explicitly excludes browser UI APIs. Read it for conventions, then keep the two surfaces separate.

Satisfy the EXISTING ControlRoomClientSurface type. Introducing a parallel client interface would leave apps/control-room's data-adapter.ts and data-contract.ts pointing at the old one, and Clause 1 would be unmet even with a working transport.
Keep each production file below 400 lines, target 250. Explicit owned paths only; no git add -A.

implementationPlan.description: Ground the seam before writing anything, because far more is committed than this task's description assumes. Read apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.ts in full, especially handleCommandRequest at :150 and its refusal order (authenticate, protocol version, decode, registry, capability, payload shape). Read http-contract.ts and write down the exact committed vocabulary you must reuse rather than restate: HTTP_BOUNDARY_ERROR_CODES, HTTP_REFUSAL_STAGES, HTTP_INPUT_BOUNDS, MAX_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_FIELDS, WIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION, Authenticator, CommandDecisionPort, and PortRefusal with its no-translation-table rule. Read event-stream.ts and note that the resumable cursor stream ALREADY EXISTS (readEventPage, resumeFromSnapshot, exported at index.ts:101) — route to it, never reimplement it. Read http-adapter.test.ts to see which boundary properties are already proven so you do not re-prove them. Confirm the only real gap with one grep: createServer(|\.listen(|Deno.serve|Bun.serve across apps, packages and adapters must return nothing. Finally read design sections 17 and 19.2 at the pinned path for the normative transport and network rulings. No files are modified.
implementationPlan.note:
Seam grounded. No files modified. Merge-base HEAD 7183c045ec563a56b285227901038320bb563ddc.

THE GAP IS CONFIRMED AND IT IS ONLY THE SOCKET. `grep -rn "createServer(|\.listen(|Deno\.serve|Bun\.serve" apps packages adapters` (node_modules excluded) returns ZERO. `apps/daemon/package.json` declares `exports: {".": "./src/index.ts"}` but NO `main` and NO `bin`, and its only scripts are typecheck and test — so the daemon is importable but not startable. Everything above the socket is already committed.

COMMITTED VOCABULARY I MUST REUSE, read rather than restated:
- `HTTP_BOUNDARY_ERROR_CODES` (6): AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, CAPABILITY_DENIED, DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH, INPUT_INVALID, INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED.
- `HTTP_REFUSAL_STAGES` (7): AUTHENTICATE, COMPATIBILITY, DECODE, REGISTRY, AUTHORIZE, PAYLOAD_SHAPE, DISPATCH.
- `HTTP_INPUT_BOUNDS` = { maxBodyBytes, maxDepth, maxPayloadFields, maxStringUtf8Bytes }, composed from MAX_JSON_* constants and `MAX_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_FIELDS = 64`. The listener reads these; it does not restate a number, so the body-bound test cannot drift from the contract.
- `WIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is DERIVED from contract constants, not a literal.

THE HANDOVER SHAPE, which decides the listener's whole job:
`HttpCommandRequest = { body: unknown; credential: string | null; protocolVersion: unknown }`. Its comment is the design constraint: **body stays RAW and undecoded, and credential and protocolVersion arrive OUT OF BAND precisely so authentication and compatibility can both answer before anything parses the body.** So the listener must NOT parse the body before delegating — reading headers and handing over raw bytes is the contract, and pre-parsing would move a decode ahead of authenticate and change the refusal order.
`HttpCommandResult = HttpAccepted | HttpPortRefused | HttpRefused`, each carrying its own `httpStatus`. So the listener serializes a status the adapter chose; it does not map codes to statuses itself.
`PortRefusal { code, detail, httpStatus, layer }` with an explicit comment that `code` and `layer` are the port's OWN values copied verbatim and that **the seam holds no translation table**. Flattening a port code into a generic boundary code is a contract violation, not a style choice.
`Authenticator.authenticate(credential: string | null)` — the listener supplies the credential and nothing more.

WHAT IS GENUINELY MINE, and it is a small set: the socket, loopback-only bind with an ephemeral port, Host validation, Origin validation, CSRF, and the body bound — because `handleCommandRequest` begins at authenticate and never sees headers. Everything from authenticate onward is committed and must be delegated. If I find myself writing a capability check, a decode, or an error-code mapping, that is duplicated authority.

TWO PREMISES IN MY OWN TASK DESCRIPTION ARE WRONG, both already caught in the architect's notes and both re-confirmed here:
1. The resumable cursor stream is NOT missing and NOT out of scope — `apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream.ts` implements it and `index.ts:101` already exports `readEventPage` and `resumeFromSnapshot`. The listener ROUTES to it; building one would be a duplicate.
2. DoD 3 is mis-specified. `ControlRoomClientSurface` (client-compat.ts:58) is a generated BUILDER REGISTRY (commands, queries, errors, pins, telemetryKinds, wireProtocolVersion), already fully implemented and already returned by `createCompatGate`. There is nothing to implement and no parallel interface may be introduced. DoD 3's intent is met by a SEND path that consumes those existing builders. This will be restated in the completion note as the plan requires.

INDEX.TS IS CONTESTED TWICE OVER — measured, and it changes step 4. It is 249 lines against a 250 target, one line of headroom. task-5e43a9e2 (Foundation daemon ingress surface, BACKLOG) exists specifically to restructure it. AND the daemon flagged a LIVE file collision at claim time: `apps/daemon/src/index.ts` is also owned by task-684e6972 (Fresh recovery incarnation and signing-key epoch), which worker-4addc779 is working RIGHT NOW. Two tasks editing a 249/250-line file concurrently is how a foreign-sweep collision happens.
So the leading option at step 4 is to NOT touch index.ts at all and export the listener from a focused module, taking the plan's own escape hatch ("if one line does not fit, export from a focused module instead and say so in the step note"). I will decide there and record it either way, but the collision makes the focused module the safer default rather than the fallback.

Next: step 2, TDD red for the listener's own boundary.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red: write the failing spec for the listener's OWN boundary — the part handleCommandRequest never sees because it begins at authenticate. Cover, each asserting a SPECIFIC stable code and naming the LISTENER as the refusing layer, since there are now two refusal layers and a test asserting only "refused" will pass when the adapter answers instead: a request whose Host header is not the bound loopback authority is refused; a request whose Origin is absent or foreign is refused; a state-changing request without a valid CSRF token is refused; a body exceeding the committed HTTP_INPUT_BOUNDS limit is refused without being fully buffered. Add the start-up spec: binding a non-loopback interface REFUSES TO START with its own code (design 19.2), binding loopback succeeds and reports the actually-bound ephemeral port, and the listener closes on every exit path including when the handler throws. Add a credential-hygiene test: no credential value appears in any emitted log line or in a URL. Read the bounds from HTTP_INPUT_BOUNDS rather than restating the numbers, so the test cannot drift from the contract. Tests fail because the listener does not exist.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED landed: apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.test.ts. No production code written.

RED EVIDENCE, and it fails for the right reason. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/http/http-listener.test.ts` -> Test Files 1 failed (1), Tests: no tests. The file cannot even reach collection because `./http-listener.js` does not exist — the missing-production-symbol failure this step is meant to retain, not a broken spec.

EVERY ASSERTION NAMES THE LAYER, NOT JUST THE CODE. There are now TWO refusal layers — this listener and the committed adapter — so `expectListenerRefusal` asserts `{ code, layer: CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER_LAYER }` together, plus that the code is a member of the frozen `LISTENER_REFUSAL_CODES`. A test asserting only "it was refused" passes when the adapter answers instead of the listener, which is precisely the detached assertion the epic rail names. The first test also pins the vocabulary itself: frozen, non-empty, no duplicates.

FIXTURES REUSED, NOT REIMPLEMENTED. `authenticator`, `decisionPort`, `registryOf`, `recordingHandler` and `envelopeObject` all come from the committed `./http-test-fixtures.js` that `http-adapter.test.ts` already uses. Nothing here builds a second authenticator or a parallel registry.

BOUNDS READ FROM THE CONTRACT, NEVER RESTATED. The oversized-body case asserts `HTTP_INPUT_BOUNDS.maxBodyBytes === MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES` first and then builds its payload from `HTTP_INPUT_BOUNDS.maxBodyBytes + 1`. No literal byte count appears, so the test cannot drift from the contract if the bound moves.

WHAT IS SPECIFIED, all of it the listener's OWN boundary — the part `handleCommandRequest` never sees because it begins at authenticate:
- Non-loopback bind REFUSES TO START with `LISTENER_NON_LOOPBACK_BIND` (design 19.2), and the refusal is asserted to carry NO `port` property, so nothing can be left listening behind a refused start.
- Loopback bind succeeds on an ephemeral port and reports the port ACTUALLY bound, so parallel runs cannot collide on a fixed port.
- `LISTENER_HOST_INVALID` for a Host that is not the bound loopback authority.
- `LISTENER_ORIGIN_INVALID` for BOTH an absent Origin and a foreign one — two separate cases, because "absent" and "wrong" are different bugs and a single case would let one regress silently.
- `LISTENER_CSRF_INVALID` for both a missing and a wrong token, same reasoning.
- `LISTENER_ROUTE_UNKNOWN` for an unknown route, asserted to be refused WITHOUT reaching the adapter.
- `LISTENER_BODY_TOO_LARGE` at the committed bound.

TWO PROPERTIES THAT ARE EASY TO ASSERT VACUOUSLY, written so they cannot be:
1. Credential hygiene. The test injects a log sink, exercises both a success and a refusal path, then asserts `lines.length > 0` BEFORE checking that no line contains the credential. Without the non-empty assertion a listener that simply logged nothing would pass while proving nothing about hygiene.
2. Cleanup on the error path. The listener is started with a handler that throws, the response is asserted to be 5xx, and then — the actual proof — a SECOND listener is started on the same explicit port and must succeed. Asserting only that `close()` resolved would pass against a leaked handle; re-binding the port is what shows the socket was really released. This matters on Windows, where a surviving handle surfaces later as EBUSY rather than as the real error.

Every started listener is closed in a `finally` via the `withListener` helper, including when the test body throws.

API SHAPE PINNED BY THE SPEC, for step 3: `startControlRoomListener({ deps, csrfToken, host?, port?, credential?, log?, onRequest? })` returning either `{ ok: true, port, origin, close() }` or a frozen refusal `{ ok: false, code, layer }`. Exports needed: `startControlRoomListener`, `ControlRoomListener`, `LISTENER_REFUSAL_CODES`, `CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER_LAYER`.

Next: step 3, the minimum node:http listener that delegates everything from authenticate onward to the committed `handleCommandRequest`.

implementationPlan.description: Make step 2 green with the minimum listener, built on node:http — add no HTTP framework dependency; the repo has none and the adapter already owns everything above the socket. The listener binds loopback only with a caller-supplied or ephemeral port, enforces Host/Origin/CSRF and the committed body bound, assembles an HttpCommandRequest, delegates to the EXISTING handleCommandRequest, and serializes the returned HttpCommandResult. It performs NO authentication, NO capability check, NO decode and NO error mapping of its own — all four are committed in the adapter, and PortRefusal's contract requires a port's code and layer to be copied verbatim rather than flattened. Route the event-stream endpoints to the existing readEventPage and resumeFromSnapshot. Keep the module under 250 lines; if it approaches that, split the header-guard logic into a sibling rather than growing it.
implementationPlan.note:
Listener implemented and its focused suite is GREEN: 10 passed (10). `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.ts` is 219 lines, under the 250 target. `.js` bridge added in the same step. Built on node:http — no HTTP framework dependency added, and the repo still has zero HTTP dependencies.

IT OWNS ONLY THE SOCKET. Route match, loopback bind, Host, Origin, CSRF and the body bound — then it assembles an `HttpCommandRequest` and delegates. No authentication, no capability check, no decode, no error mapping: all four are committed in `handleCommandRequest`, and the adapter's own `httpStatus` is serialized verbatim rather than re-derived. `PortRefusal`'s no-translation-table rule is respected because the listener never inspects an adapter result — it forwards it.

The body is passed RAW. `HttpCommandRequest`'s contract puts `credential` and `protocolVersion` out of band precisely so authenticate and compatibility can answer before anything parses; pre-parsing in the transport would move a decode ahead of authenticate and silently change the committed refusal order.

A REAL TEST DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED, AND IT WOULD HAVE MADE THE HOST GUARD UNTESTABLE. My first version drove requests with `fetch`. The Host case failed with `stage: "AUTHENTICATE"` — the ADAPTER answering, not the listener. Cause: undici treats `Host` as a forbidden header and drops it silently, so the request arrived carrying the real authority and sailed through the guard.

Why that matters beyond one red test: with `fetch`, a listener with NO Host check at all produces the same result. The test could not distinguish a working guard from a missing one — it was incapable of ever proving the property. Rewritten to use `node:http` with `setHost: false` so the header is actually settable. Worth carrying: **a header-validation test written with `fetch` is vacuous for any forbidden header** (Host, Connection, Content-Length among others).

DEFENSIVE CHOICES, each against a specific failure:
- Only `127.0.0.1` and `::1` may be bound, and a HOSTNAME is not accepted — a name could resolve off-loopback, which is the same exposure by a slower route. Non-loopback REFUSES TO START per design 19.2, and the refusal carries no `port`, so nothing is left listening behind it.
- The body bound stops reading AT the limit rather than buffering first and measuring after; a limit enforced after the bytes are in memory is not a limit.
- Absent and foreign Origin are both refused. A missing Origin is not a safe default for a state-changing request.
- The log line emits method and path with the query string stripped, and never the credential (design 19.2: credentials never in URLs or logs).
- `closeAllConnections()` before `close()`, and the failure path closes a half-bound server too — on Windows a surviving handle surfaces later as EBUSY rather than as the real error.

PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE — THE DAEMON SUITE IS RED AND NONE OF IT IS MINE. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`: 1 file failed / 27 passed, 63 failed / 495 passed. Every one of the 63 failures is in `src/recovery/recovery-incarnation.test.ts`, which is UNTRACKED and belongs to task-684e6972 (Fresh recovery incarnation and signing-key epoch), in flight with worker-4addc779 right now. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` fails on the same file: `src/recovery/recovery-incarnation.test.ts(545,40): error TS2339: Property 'CryptoKey' does not exist on type 'Crypto'.`

Intersection with my owned paths is EMPTY: `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/http/` shows only my three new files. Reported verbatim, not hidden and not claimed. This will be re-measured at step 8 against the merge-base set rather than carried forward from here.

Next: step 4, make the daemon startable (manifest entry point) without touching index.ts.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red: write the failing spec for the client send path. IMPORTANT CORRECTION, to be recorded in the completion note: this task's DoD 3 says to implement the EXISTING ControlRoomClientSurface, but that type (client-compat.ts:58) is a generated BUILDER REGISTRY — commands, queries, errors, pins, telemetryKinds, wireProtocolVersion — already fully implemented and returned by createCompatGate. There is nothing to implement and no parallel interface may be introduced. DoD 3's intent is satisfied instead by a send function that CONSUMES those existing builders. Specify it that way: given an envelope produced by GENERATED_COMMAND_BUILDERS or a query builder, it performs the round trip and returns the daemon's result unchanged. Assert that a daemon refusal is surfaced with the daemon's OWN code and layer, not re-coded client-side; that a transport failure is distinguishable from a daemon refusal by a distinct stable code; and that the credential is sent in a header, never in a URL. Tests fail because the module does not exist.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED landed: packages/control-room-client/src/client-transport.test.ts. No production code written.

RED EVIDENCE, failing for the right reason: "Error: Cannot find module './client-transport.js'" -> Test Files 1 failed (1), Tests: no tests.

DoD 3 CORRECTION CONFIRMED ON DISK, exactly as the architect predicted. client-compat.ts:58 ControlRoomClientSurface = { commands, errors, pins, queries, telemetryKinds, wireProtocolVersion } — a generated BUILDER REGISTRY, already fully implemented and already returned by createCompatGate. Nothing to implement, and introducing a parallel client interface is forbidden. The spec therefore pins a SEND path that CONSUMES the builders: every envelope in the suite comes from GENERATED_COMMAND_BUILDERS["goal.create"] applied to an affordance built by the real contracts parser (buildNextAllowedCommands), and one case asserts the transported body deep-equals that builder output — a hand-rolled or reshaped envelope reddens.

Shape specified: delivered:true carries the daemon's answer verbatim (response + status); delivered:false carries this layer's OWN code. That split is what makes "the daemon refused" and "we never got an answer" impossible to confuse. Two transport codes, both distinct from any daemon code: TRANSPORT_REQUEST_FAILED (fetch rejected) and TRANSPORT_RESPONSE_UNREADABLE (answer was not JSON). The no-translation-table rule is asserted directly: on a 401 the response deep-equals the daemon's own {error:{code:"AUTHENTICATION_FAILED"}, stage:"AUTHENTICATE"} object AND the test asserts AUTHENTICATION_FAILED is not a member of TRANSPORT_REFUSAL_CODES.

Credential hygiene (design 19.2) asserted positively and negatively: the FULL url must equal `${origin}/command`, so a path-embedded token fails as well as a query string; the url must not contain the credential; and the credential must appear in the x-moe-session-credential header. The protocol-version header is read from GENERATED_WIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION rather than restated, so client and daemon cannot drift.

TWO REAL DEFECTS IN MY OWN STEP-3 LISTENER, found while writing this spec, both invisible to the step-3 suite because it only ever asserted LISTENER-layer refusals and never completed one round trip:
1. BODY TYPE. The listener passes a string to handleCommandRequest, but decodeRuntimeCommandEnvelopeBytes -> decodeBoundedJsonBytes -> snapshotBytes requires a Uint8Array: "if (types.isProxy(input) || !types.isUint8Array(input)) return failure('JSON_INPUT_TYPE_INVALID')". Every real command would have refused at DECODE. Fixed in step 6.
2. CREDENTIAL SOURCE. The listener reads the credential from a per-LISTENER option, not from the request, so every caller on a listener would share one credential. It must come from the x-moe-session-credential header. Fixed in step 6, and the log-hygiene test is strengthened to send the credential the real way.
Also outstanding from step 3: the event-stream routes were described in that step's note but never implemented — serve() routes only /command. DoD 2 and DoD 4 need the committed READ surface, so /events/read is added in step 6 delegating to the existing readEventPage(port, request); the seam reimplements nothing.

Client route surface specified: sendCommand -> POST /command, readEventPage -> POST /events/read. The request shape {limit?, projection, subscriberId} is declared locally in the client because packages/control-room-client cannot depend on apps/daemon without inverting the architecture's dependency arrow; it is structurally the committed EventReadRequest at event-stream-contract.ts:162.

THE EQUALITY IS THE TEST, not a 200. A started daemon serves the committed READ over the socket; the same EventReadRequest is then run through the in-process readEventPage against a FRESH streamPort, and the transported payload must deep-equal it. A transport that dropped, renamed, reordered or re-typed a single field fails even though the request would still have "worked". Two guards against a vacuous pass: separate port instances per side, so a stateful double cannot mutate the baseline it is compared against, and explicit assertions that the in-process frame really is outcome PAGE with a non-empty events array — otherwise two empty objects would compare equal and prove nothing.

THE ROUND TRIP CAUGHT WHAT THE UNIT SUITES COULD NOT. The command leg returns outcome ACCEPTED. Before step 6's byte fix the listener handed the adapter a string, so every well-formed command refused at DECODE with JSON_INPUT_TYPE_INVALID while the socket still looked perfectly healthy — exactly the failure a responsiveness test cannot see.

NEGATIVE LEGS, each naming WHICH of the two layers refused. Unknown route: real fetch to /not-a-route returns 404 with body deep-equal to { code: "LISTENER_ROUTE_UNKNOWN", layer: "CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER" }. Malformed body on /command with every header valid: refused with stage DECODE by the committed ADAPTER, asserted as such — that assertion is what proves the listener did not pre-empt a check the adapter already owns. These two cases refusing at different layers is the point; a test asserting only "non-200" would pass with either.

CONSUMER EDGE IS REAL, not exports. The client is built through createCompatGate exactly as production must: the envelope comes from gate.client.commands["goal.create"] and wireProtocolVersion from gate.client, so the tested configuration is the only one reachable past the pin check.

DESIGN RULINGS, both verified against the pinned doc (sha256 matches the epic rail):
- Section 17: "The control room uses authenticated HTTP commands/queries plus a resumable cursor stream"; HTTP, MCP, UI and IDE use the SAME generated command ID/schema.
- Section 19.2: "Loopback is the only default bind. UI sessions use OS-protected bootstrap material, secure same-site cookies, CSRF token, and strict Host/Origin validation. Credentials never appear in URLs or logs. Non-loopback refuses to start unless a reviewed policy explicitly enables authenticated transport security and allowed origins/hosts."
- Section 19.1 bounds tested at N and N+1: command body 1 MiB, canonical JSON depth 64. HTTP_INPUT_BOUNDS already encodes these — read them, do not restate them.
planningNotes.risks:
1. DO NOT REIMPLEMENT THE BOUNDARY. Everything from authenticate onward is committed in handleCommandRequest. The listener's job stops at building an HttpCommandRequest and serializing the HttpCommandResult. If you find yourself writing a capability check, a decode, or an error-code mapping, you are duplicating authority — and PortRefusal's comment is explicit that the seam holds no translation table and copies a port's own code and layer verbatim.

2. HOST/ORIGIN/CSRF IS GENUINELY NEW AND IS YOURS. handleCommandRequest begins at authenticate; it never sees headers. Section 19.2 requires strict Host/Origin validation and a CSRF token, so the listener must enforce them BEFORE delegating, with its own stable codes and its own refusal stage. Test each with the specific code, and name which layer refused — there are now two refusal layers (listener and adapter) and a test asserting only "it was refused" will silently pass when the wrong one answers.

3. NON-LOOPBACK MUST REFUSE TO START, not warn. Section 19.2 is unambiguous. A dev-convenience bind to 0.0.0.0 on a machine that also runs agent processes is a real exposure, not a nit.

4. CREDENTIALS NEVER IN URLS OR LOGS (section 19.2). Put the credential in a header or cookie, never a query string, and assert no log line contains it. This is easy to violate accidentally by logging a whole request object.

5. INDEX.TS IS AT 249 OF 250 LINES AND IS CONTESTED. task-5e43a9e294ef48fdab23817c8c6cfc45 (Foundation daemon ingress surface, BACKLOG) exists specifically to extract a focused surface from it. Add at most a single export line, or export the listener from a focused module instead. Coordinate before restructuring index.ts — that is that task's job, not this one's.

6. LEAKED LISTENERS ARE THE CLASSIC FAILURE. Close on every exit path including throw. Use an ephemeral port so parallel runs cannot collide; on Windows a surviving handle surfaces later as EBUSY rather than the real error.

7. DO NOT DUPLICATE packages/mcp/src/http/**. That adapter is DONE, serves MCP hosts, and explicitly excludes browser UI APIs. Read it for conventions only.

8. The equality assertion in DoD 4 is the whole point of the task: transported payload must equal the in-process handler's payload for the same input. A test that only asserts a 200 proves the socket works, not that the transport is faithful.
